findings.title: One individual had excessive control over the Maryland Trauma Physician Services Fund.
findings.description: The Maryland Health Care Commission (MHCC) had not established sufficient controls over the Maryland Trauma Physician Services Fund. One individual had excessive control over the Fund’s recordkeeping, collections, and payments, and checks were not restrictively endorsed immediately upon receipt.

dollar_amounts.context: checks received to reimburse the Fund

findings.recommendation: separate the duties for Fund recordkeeping, collection, and payment; and restrictively endorsed checks immediately upon receipt.

findings.title: Grant agreements were not always executed prior to disbursing funds and certain healthcare grants were not adequately monitored.
findings.description: The Maryland Community Health Resources Commission (MCHRC) did not always execute grant agreements prior to disbursing funds and did not adequately monitor certain healthcare grants. MCHRC did not document its review of self-reported grantee performance results and did not always obtain supporting documentation for reported expenditures.

dollar_amounts.context: not signed by MCHRC prior to approving grant payments
remaining 2 grant agreements... were not signed
reported grant expenditures related to 7 of the grants without supporting documentation
supporting documentation for certain reported grant expenditures was not sufficient

findings.recommendation: ensure all grant agreements are properly executed prior to making payments to the grantees; perform a documented review of self-reported grantee performance results and expenditure reports; obtain supporting documentation, at least on a test basis...

extraction.agency_response_summary: The agencies concurred with all recommendations. MHCC implemented a formal process for separation of duties effective December 1, 2014. MCHRC agreed to execute agreements prior to payment and perform documented reviews immediately, with supporting documentation testing beginning May 1, 2015.
